summary: Header normalization at edge causes model-version-binding drift and unexpected fallback routing for tenant
description:
Issue summary:
A Clarion Health tenant observed repeated fallbacks to the older model variant during a controlled canary shift. The customer had explicitly pinned sessions to rw-open-13b-v2 for regulatory consistency, but a subset of long-running sessions began receiving rw-open-7b-quant responses.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests for the tenant in us-east-1 were served by the legacy model over a 45-minute window (confirmed by token/log sampling).
- Some responses had degraded length/formatting; Clarion flagged this as a potential regression for clinical note generation.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (Clarion reserved capacity) in us-east-1
- Customer pinned model via tenant routing metadata header: X-Tenant-Model-Version: rw-open-13b-v2
- Deployment was performing a canary weight shift from 5% to 20% at the time

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a long-running streaming session with pinned_version header set to rw-open-13b-v2.
2) Continue with multi-part streaming prompts over ~20 minutes.
3) Trigger a canary weight bump (internal rollout).
4) Observe occasional responses produced by rw-open-7b-quant and session affinity logs showing routing to fallback variant.

Observed behavior:
- Edge logs show header normalization path rewriting X-Tenant-Model-Version to x-tenant-model-version (lowercased) for some streaming frames.
- Routing mesh relies on exact-match binding token produced by the control-plane handshake; when header key case changes mid-session, the binding token calculated at the ingress no longer matches the control-plane pin state and the request is routed via fallback logic.
- No 5xx errors; requests succeeded but hit wrong variant.

Expected behavior:
- Header case normalization at the proxy should be transparent to model-binding logic (control-plane should use header values case-insensitively or preserve the original header token across handshake).

Business impact:
- Customer paused an internal rollout until guaranteed pin stability.
- Regulatory/process concern: model drift for generated clinical text could require audit and rollback for affected outputs.

Attachments & logs:
- Sample request/response IDs: req-ccf4a6e1, req-ccf4b90a, req-ccf4d2b0
- Edge trace: https://observability.redwood/trace/ccf4a6e1
- Routing decision timeline: https://dashboards.redwood/d/tenant-routing/clarion-135791
- Slack thread: #support-clarion-health (ts: 2026-03-10T18:05:00Z)
comments: 2026-03-10 18:12 Aisha Kapoor: Initial report from Clarion Health attached; they provided token-sampled responses showing variant mismatch. Escalating due to customer_tier=dedeicated and compliance surface.

2026-03-10 18:27 Marco Chen: Assigned. Reproduced locally against staging edge-proxy with streaming frames; saw header key lowercased in the proxy's buffered chunk handler. Adding SRE and Edge owners.

2026-03-11 09:14 Lydia Park (SRE): Confirmed that the proxy's normalization config was recently modified by PR 998 to canonicalize header keys. Hypothesis: normalization runs mid-stream when chunk boundaries align with header frame splits.

2026-03-11 11:40 Marco Chen: Added a temporary routing shim to treat pinned header keys case-insensitively at control-plane match stage. Patch applied to staging routing mesh for validation (PR 1428). Monitoring behavior under canary weight shift test.

2026-03-12 07:55 Clarion Health (Customer): After the staging test, they reported no further variant drift in a 2-hour smoke test. They've requested a production mitigation and a permanent fix to ensure auditability.

2026-03-12 12:02 Marco Chen: Noted next steps: (1) fast rollback of header canonicalization in edge-proxy (hotfix), (2) add idempotent case-insensitive header matching to control-plane binding, (3) add e2e test for streaming chunked headers. Scheduling patch windows with infra team.
investigation_notes: Edge proxy change (PR 998) introduced header canonicalization to prevent a separate routing bug; work runs per-chunk and can mutate header keys mid-stream.
Control-plane binding uses the raw header key name as part of the session affinity token; token generation assumed header key stability.
Sampling of logs shows mismatches correlate with streaming sessions longer than ~15 minutes and with chunk sizes that split header metadata across multiple frames.
No evidence of traffic loss or 5xx; only routing decision divergence leading to fallback to compatible variant.
Staging patch (PR 1428) that makes control-plane header matching case-insensitive removed the mismatch in simulated runs.
Potential edge cases: other middleware that mutates header payloads (trailing whitespace, quoting) could produce similar token mismatches; need to harden token derivation.
resolution: Workaround applied: staged case-insensitive matching in routing mesh (PR 1428) rolled to a canary group to prevent further pin divergence. Hotfix plan: revert canonicalization behavior in edge-proxy that mutates header keys mid-stream (edge-proxy PR 1001), and implement robust canonical token derivation in control-plane (PR 1430). Follow-ups: add regression test that simulates chunked streaming headers and an audit log entry for any header normalization events. Customer requested confirmation and a postmortem; SRE will run a 72-hour observation window before closing.
